findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — [P1, confidence 100] `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` changes a live Redis key from Set to Sorted Set without a versioned key or transition, so every buffer that encounters a pre-deploy `span-buf:s:*` Set raises WRONGTYPE and drops its span-ingestion batch until that key expires.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — [P1, confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` applies numeric rounding to AuditLogEntry.datetime after organization_auditlogs selects this paginator, so an authorized `optimized_pagination=true` request crashes while building its cursor instead of returning the audit-log page.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — [P2, confidence 100] `for i = 0, 1000 do` truncates redirect resolution at one tenth of the established 10,000-hop bound, so a trace whose segment tree exceeds 1,000 levels is joined into the wrong buffer and flushes as fragmented segments.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — [P1][confidence 100] `if span_count > 1000 then` has no test that inserts more than 1,000 spans into one buffer and verifies eviction retains the intended score-ordered 1,000 spans, so a regression in the task’s required insert-time eviction behavior ships undetected.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1, confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the `AuditLogEntry.datetime` value selected by `order_by="-datetime"`, raising `TypeError` and returning 500 for every authorized `optimized_pagination=true` request.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — [P1, confidence 100] `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` changes the organization audit-log API with an administrator-only pagination mode even though the accepted task is solely "Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert," so the final artifact departs from its stated objective without human acceptance.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — Confidence 100, Severity P1: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError for the `datetime` values selected by the optimized audit-log endpoint, so an authorized `optimized_pagination=true` request with any audit-log row returns a raw 500.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Confidence 100, Severity P1: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes the accepted cursor offset from `0:-1:1` into a negative Django QuerySet slice, which raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` and turns the list request into a raw 500.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Confidence 100, Severity P1: `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` raises Redis `WRONGTYPE` for every still-live pre-deploy `span-buf:s:*` Set, aborting the consumer batch instead of handling the one-hour compatibility window while buffered spans remain in Redis.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` introduces an administrator-selectable audit-log pagination feature that is unrelated to the stated task, “Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert,” expanding the change into an unapproved API/paginator feature.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — [P1, confidence 100] `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0` is added only to fixtures containing at most five identically scored spans, so the `zpopmin` eviction branch for a segment above 1000 spans and its requirement to retain the newest spans are never exercised and regressions ship green.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — [P1, confidence 100] `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` introduces an administrator-only paginator branch with no diff test that sends `optimized_pagination=true` for either authorized or unauthorized users, so its pagination, authorization, and fallback behavior can break while the changed spans-only tests pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — [P1, confidence 100] `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` changes a live Redis key from Set to Sorted Set without a versioned key or transition, so every buffer that encounters a pre-deploy `span-buf:s:*` Set raises WRONGTYPE and drops its span-ingestion batch until that key expires.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows buffer.py changing from `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` to `p.zadd(set_key, ...)` at line 197, and from `p.sscan` to `p.zscan` at line 431. The key pattern `span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{parent_span_id}` remains the same. During deployment, existing Redis keys created with SADD (Set type) will still exist, but the new code will try to use ZADD/ZSCAN (Sorted Set operations) on them. Redis will return WRONGTYPE error when attempting sorted set operations on a set key. This is a real migration issue - there's no versioned key change or transition logic to handle existing Set keys.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — [P2, confidence 100] `for i = 0, 1000 do` truncates redirect resolution at one tenth of the established 10,000-hop bound, so a trace whose segment tree exceeds 1,000 levels is joined into the wrong buffer and flushes as fragmented segments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being changed from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, traces with segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now fail to be joined correctly, causing fragmented segments. This is a real behavioral change that could cause data integrity issues for deep traces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — Confidence 100, Severity P1: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError for the `datetime` values selected by the optimized audit-log endpoint, so an authorized `optimized_pagination=true` request with any audit-log row returns a raw 500.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, the OptimizedCursorPaginator is used for audit logs with `order_by="-datetime"`. The `get_item_key` method at line 840 does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`. The `value` comes from `getattr(item, self.key)` where `self.key` is derived from the order_by field, which would be 'datetime'. A datetime object cannot be passed to `math.floor()` or `math.ceil()` - these functions require numeric types. This would raise a TypeError when trying to paginate audit log results that have datetime fields, causing a 500 error for authorized users making optimized_pagination=true requests.
